rationale: The candidate reads as a coherent compact neighborhood building with a dominant stepped mass and a legible carved open center. The isometric, opposite, front, and top views agree on the same general rule: a low-to-midrise block is not merely stacked, but organized around an internal courtyard/void with one side opened toward the access edge. The top view especially confirms that the mass is not just a filled rectangle; it is a C/U-shaped figure with a clear open center, which supports the brief for active ground and public threshold. The silhouette is stepped, but not as a random cake; it behaves like a continuous occupied terrace mass with a clear hierarchy. It also resonates with the reference set through courtyard/public-void logic rather than through facade style. Program fit is strong for neighborhood living / 근린생활시설 because the mass can plausibly host mixed neighborhood uses, public edge exchange, and upper-level hierarchy without requiring a long-span section. The only caution is that the section remains somewhat generic and box-derived; it could be more explicitly profiled or articulated if the next iteration needs stronger section character, but it is not a hard failure.
